explanation_short: KNN consistently shows the highest R² values, peaking at n=9 (0.83014) and maintaining high performance (0.81786) at n=11. RF shows the best overall trend, achieving its peak R² at n=11 (0.78554) and having the lowest MSE (0.01503) at this point. SVM and XGBoost both peak at n=4, suggesting a potential optimal feature set size for these models.
explanation_full: The best feature-count step per model highlights the optimal feature subset size for each algorithm. KNN achieves its best performance with 9 features (R²=0.83014, MSE=0.01190), suggesting that the inclusion of the first 9 features (VFA through ORP_Low) is most critical for its predictive power. RF shows the best overall performance at n=11 (R²=0.78554, MSE=0.01503), indicating that incorporating all 11 features yields the best result for this model. SVM and XGBoost both identify n=4 as their optimal feature count, suggesting that the initial set of 4 features (VFA -> Butyrate -> Acetate -> VSS) captures the most predictive information for these models. DT's best performance is at n=9 (R²=0.67143, MSE=0.02302), which is better than its performance at n=11 (R²=0.61060, MSE=0.02728). The comparison shows that while KNN and RF benefit from adding more features up to n=11, SVM and XGBoost benefit most from a smaller, initial set of 4 features.
